When a research question calls for calculations and figures—not just prose—
Tempest can pair a completed STORM report or Co-STORM session with reproducible
R analyses and conceptual illustrations. The original research remains the
evidence authority while `tempest_enrich_report()` produces a separate,
self-contained HTML article and integrity-checked bundle.

<div class="tempest-callout">
<strong>Inspect a published live report:</strong> see the
<a href="../live-research/index.html">hosted CO2 grass experiment report</a>
with executed charts, downloadable CSVs, source notes, and provenance records.
</div>

## Launch the Researcher app

`tempest_researcher_app()` wraps this workflow in a dedicated Shiny app with
starter briefs, optional R code execution and image generation, selectable host
tools and MCP servers, a searchable library of saved reports, and optional
Graft project memory:

```{r researcher-app, eval = FALSE}
library(tempest)

tempest_researcher_app(
  output_dir = "research-reports",
  report_library = TRUE,
  graft_store = "research-memory"
)
```

Key capabilities in the app:

- **Editable starter briefs**: pick a template (evidence comparison, public-data
  analysis, or visual explainer), edit the prompt, and launch research in an
  isolated background R process that you can cancel cleanly at any time.
- **Evidence navigator**: inspect recorded sources alongside which analysis and
  illustration tasks succeeded, failed, or were skipped.
- **Saved-report library (`report_library = TRUE`)**: search and reopen
  previously published reports for reading or ZIP download. When `graft_store`
  is set, each report displays its live Graft status (`Accepted`, `Provisional`,
  `Superseded`, or `Withdrawn`).
- **Project memory (`graft_store = ...`)**: review any completed report and
  explicitly accept it into a named Graft stream, record a correction, or
  withdraw it. New runs can consult accepted streams through read-only
  `graft::graft_tools()` or pin one stream as a comparison basis.
- **Ragnar corpus support**: if `config` includes a `ragnar` store, each job
  runs against a private copy of the existing corpus so runs stay isolated and
  never corrupt the host database.

### Connect custom R tools and MCP servers

Pass named zero-argument tool factories via `tools` so experts can query local
datasets or internal APIs under Deputy's read-only research permissions:

```{r researcher-app-tools, eval = FALSE}
tempest_researcher_app(
  tools = list(plant_data = function() {
    list(ellmer::tool(
      function() as.data.frame(datasets::CO2),
      name = "read_co2_data",
      description = "Read the built-in CO2 plant experiment data",
      arguments = list(),
      annotations = ellmer::tool_annotations(
        read_only_hint = TRUE,
        open_world_hint = FALSE
      )
    ))
  }),
  mcp_config = "mcp.json",
  output_dir = "research-reports",
  report_library = TRUE,
  graft_store = "research-memory"
)
```

For MCP servers, supply `mcp_config = "mcp.json"` (or upload a JSON file in the
sidebar). Discovery lists available tools without enabling them; only servers
owning the tools you explicitly select are connected when research starts.

## Scripted workflow: `tempest_researcher()`

From R scripts, call `tempest_researcher()` to run STORM and enrich the result
in one step. Code execution (`allow_code = FALSE`) and image generation stay
opt-in—you can inspect the proposed `plan.json` and scripts first, then re-run
`tempest_enrich_report()` with a reviewed plan and `allow_code = TRUE`:

```{r live-researcher, eval = FALSE}
result <- tempest_researcher(
  "How does overnight chilling relate to CO2 uptake in Echinochloa crus-galli?",
  output_dir = "live-co2-enriched-report",
  config = tempest_config(),
  max_questions_per_perspective = 2L,
  enrichment = list(
    executor = tempest_r_executor(timeout = 120),
    image_generator = tempest_image_generator(),
    allow_code = FALSE,
    max_analyses = 2L,
    max_illustrations = 1L
  )
)

result$research # Canonical completed STORM product
result$report   # Separate, integrity-checked enriched report
```

Verify any saved report directory later with `tempest_read_enriched_report()`,
which checks every declared file against its SHA-256 digest in `manifest.json`:

```{r read-report, eval = FALSE}
checked <- tempest_read_enriched_report(result$report@path)
checked@status
```

## Worked offline example: `datasets::CO2`

The package includes a complete offline replay under
`inst/examples/enriched-research/` analyzing chilling treatment and carbon
uptake in *Echinochloa crus-galli* (`datasets::CO2`). The numerical R analyses
are real computations; the STORM dialogue is a deterministic replay fixture so
you can inspect the entire pipeline without credentials or network access.

### Study design notes

The [R `datasets::CO2` help page](https://www.stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/datasets/html/zCO2.html)
contains 84 rows across 12 plants (six Quebec, six Mississippi) measured over
seven ambient CO2 concentrations. The original paper by Potvin, Lechowicz, and
Tardif (1990), [*The Statistical Analysis of Ecophysiological Response Curves
Obtained from Experiments Involving Repeated Measures*](https://doi.org/10.2307/1938276),
establishes three details the worked example preserves explicitly:

- Control and chilled plants were paired within origin before treatment
  (Quebec: `Qn1–Qc3`, `Qn2–Qc1`, `Qn3–Qc2`; Mississippi: `Mn1–Mc3`, `Mn2–Mc2`,
  `Mn3–Mc1`), so repeated concentrations are not treated as independent plants.
- Table 1 in the [authors' copy](https://biology.mcgill.ca/faculty/potvin/articles/PotvinLech_90.pdf)
  labels concentration in µL/L (whereas the R help page says mL/L) and sets the
  first level to 95 (Methods prose mentions 100); the example flags both
  discrepancies explicitly.
- Methods specify chilling as 14 hours at 7°C followed by 10 hours of recovery
  at 20°C (the R help summarizes this as "chilled overnight").

### Executed paired contrasts

The bundled scripts compute within-origin paired chilled-minus-control
differences at the highest concentration and across the trapezoidal response
curve area, with 20,000-draw seeded percentile bootstrap intervals
(`seed = 20261114`). With only three pairs per origin, these intervals are
descriptive summaries of this dataset rather than population-level inference:

| Quantity | Estimate | 95% bootstrap interval |
|---|---:|---:|
| Highest level, Quebec chilled − control (µmol m⁻² s⁻¹) | −2.33 | [−5.60, 1.70] |
| Highest level, Mississippi chilled − control (µmol m⁻² s⁻¹) | −12.87 | [−17.10, −5.90] |
| Highest level, equal-origin average (µmol m⁻² s⁻¹) | −7.60 | [−10.68, −4.12] |
| Highest-level interaction (Mississippi − Quebec) | −10.53 | [−16.70, −3.57] |
| Integrated curve, Quebec chilled − control (µmol m⁻² s⁻¹ × µL/L) | −3236.6 | [−5445.2, 85.5] |
| Integrated curve, Mississippi chilled − control (µmol m⁻² s⁻¹ × µL/L) | −10579.1 | [−15307.2, −6075.8] |
| Integrated-curve interaction (Mississippi − Quebec) | −7342.5 | [−12263.2, −2421.8] |

### Run the offline example yourself

```{r reproduce, eval = FALSE}
example_dir <- system.file("examples", "enriched-research", package = "tempest")
list.files(example_dir, recursive = TRUE)

system2(
  file.path(R.home("bin"), "Rscript"),
  c(file.path(example_dir, "run-example.R"), "co2-enriched-report")
)
```

The driver builds a deterministic plan naming exact `source_ids` from
`tempest_sources(research)$id`, executes the two bundled R scripts via
`tempest_r_executor()`, attaches the bundled conceptual illustration labeled
clearly as artwork rather than evidence, and validates the output bundle with
`tempest_read_enriched_report()`.

### About the hosted live qualification report

The [hosted reader edition](../live-research/index.html) was produced from a
supervised live run (`gpt-6.1-sol` + `gpt-image-2.6-flare`) with human review
of the OCR'd 1990 source, analysis plan, and synthesis rounding. Its descriptive
unpaired group averages across all seven concentrations are **−10.14** for
Mississippi and **−3.58** for Quebec (µmol m⁻² s⁻¹)—distinct from the paired
contrasts in the offline example above. Every review step and limitation is
recorded alongside the hosted report.
